ports.name: items
ports.description: The list to run the template once for; each entry becomes one task and is passed to it as a record

ports.name: stopOnFailure
ports.description: Abandons the remaining items as soon as one task fails, rather than running the whole list

ports.name: maxRunningTasks
ports.description: How many tasks may run at the same time; must be at least 1 or the run fails rather than starting

ports.name: taskTemplate
ports.description: The component to run once per item, which must expose the ports named under Template Contract

ports.name: taskStartInput
ports.description: Name of the template's signal input to pulse when a task begins

ports.name: taskSuccessOutput
ports.description: Name of the template's signal output that means one task finished successfully

ports.name: taskFailureOutput
ports.description: Name of the template's signal output that means one task failed

ports.name: taskErrorOutput
ports.description: Name of an optional value output on the template carrying why a task failed; leave blank if it cannot say

ports.name: run
ports.description: Starts a run over Items; a Do while a run is already in progress reports Unchanged rather than queueing

ports.name: abort
ports.description: Stops starting new tasks and ends the run once those already running finish; reports Unchanged when no run is in progress

ports.name: aborted
ports.description: Fires when a run ended early, either from Abort or because Stop On Failure caught a failure

ports.name: done
ports.description: Fires when the run ended having done its work: every task completed without failing, the Items list was empty, or an Abort was honoured — Aborted fires alongside it when the run ended early

ports.name: completed
ports.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

ports.name: unchanged
ports.description: Fires when there was nothing to do: a Do while a run is already in progress, or an Abort with no run in progress

ports.name: failure
ports.description: Fires when at least one task failed, or when the run could not start at all; which item failed is reported on the error channel

ports.tooltip: What a Send does while the connection is not open. Queue holds it (in order) until the socket reopens; Drop discards it and counts it; Report Error also sets Last Error and fires On Error.

ports.name: maxQueueSize
ports.description: Messages the queue holds before further Sends are refused and counted as dropped; 0 or less is unlimited and can grow during a long outage
ports.tooltip: Messages the queue holds before further Sends are refused and counted in Dropped. 0 or less means unlimited, which can grow without bound during a long outage.

ports.name: connectionState
ports.description: Where the connection is: idle, connecting, open, reconnecting, closed or error

ports.name: connected
ports.description: True only while the socket is open and messages can be sent without queueing

ports.name: retryCount
ports.description: Attempts made during the current outage; back to zero once the socket opens

ports.name: lastError
ports.description: What went wrong most recently, including why a reconnect was scheduled or abandoned

ports.name: queueSize
ports.description: Messages held because the socket was not open when Send ran

ports.name: droppedCount
ports.description: Messages that will never be sent, whether discarded by policy, by a full queue, or by the node being removed

ports.name: latency
ports.description: Round trip of the last heartbeat in milliseconds; 0 until one has been measured

ports.name: closeCode
ports.description: WebSocket close code from the last close, or 1006 when the socket died without one

ports.name: closeReason
ports.description: Reason the server gave for closing, which is often blank

ports.name: received
ports.description: The last message, parsed as JSON when it is JSON and handed over as text when it is not

ports.name: receivedRaw
ports.description: The last text message exactly as it arrived; blank for a binary frame

ports.name: receivedIsBinary
ports.description: True when the last message was a binary frame, in which case Received holds the buffer

ports.name: onOpen
ports.description: Fires every time the socket opens, including after a reconnect

ports.name: onMessage
ports.description: Fires once per message, after Received already holds it; heartbeat replies are not messages

ports.name: onMessageSent
ports.description: Fires when a message has been handed to the socket, including a queued one flushed on reopen; not for heartbeats

ports.name: onError
ports.description: Fires when something went wrong: a failed connect, a refused send, a dead heartbeat, or a give-up

ports.name: onClose
ports.description: Fires whenever the socket goes down, whether or not a reconnect is going to follow

ports.name: onReconnect
ports.description: Fires on every open after the first; a WebSocket cannot resume, so this is the cue to re-fetch rather than assume continuity

ports.name: done
ports.description: Fires when the action finished: a Connect whose socket opened, a Send accepted for delivery (sent, or queued for the next open), or a Disconnect that closed something

ports.name: completed
ports.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

ports.name: unchanged
ports.description: Fires when there was nothing to do: a Disconnect with nothing open, a Send discarded by the Drop policy, or a Connect a later Connect or Disconnect superseded before it opened

ports.name: failure
ports.description: Fires when the action could not be performed — no URL, a URL that is not ws:// or wss://, a connection that gave up, or a refused Send. Last Error carries the reason

ports.name: url
ports.description: Endpoint to stream from; changing it while connected reconnects to the new one

ports.name: transport
ports.description: How the stream is fetched: Fetch carries headers and a body, EventSource lets the browser handle reconnection, Auto prefers Fetch

ports.name: method
ports.description: HTTP method for the request; anything other than GET needs the Fetch transport

ports.name: headers
ports.description: Request headers as an object, for bearer tokens and the like; ignored by the EventSource transport, which cannot set them

ports.name: body
ports.description: Request body, sent as JSON unless it is already a string; ignored for GET and HEAD

ports.name: withCredentials
ports.description: Sends cookies and HTTP auth to a cross-origin endpoint, which the server must also allow

ports.name: eventTypes
ports.description: Comma-separated named event types to subscribe to; only needed for the EventSource transport, as Fetch delivers every type
ports.tooltip: Comma-separated named event types to subscribe to. Only needed for the EventSource transport, which delivers a named event only to a listener registered in advance; the Fetch transport delivers every event type.

ports.name: textPath
ports.description: Where the text lives inside a JSON payload, as a dot path such as choices.0.delta.content; leave blank for a stream of bare text
ports.tooltip: Where the text lives inside a JSON payload, as a dot path — for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, choices.0.delta.content. Leave blank for a stream that sends bare text. Whatever it names ends up on the Text output, which is always a string.

ports.name: autoConnect
ports.description: Opens the stream as soon as a URL is available, without waiting for a Connect signal

ports.name: autoReconnect
ports.description: Retries after a failure with a growing backoff; turning it off reports the failure and stops

ports.name: reconnectOnStreamEnd
ports.description: Reconnects when the server closes the stream cleanly; off by default because reconnecting an agent stream re-issues the request
ports.tooltip: Reconnect when the server closes the stream cleanly. Off by default: an agent response stream is finite, and reconnecting would re-issue the request and start the response again.

ports.name: reconnectDelay
ports.description: First retry delay in milliseconds, doubling per consecutive failure up to Max Reconnect Delay
ports.tooltip: First retry delay. Doubles per consecutive failure, up to the maximum.

ports.name: maxReconnectDelay
ports.description: Ceiling on the backoff in milliseconds, however many failures there have been

ports.name: maxRetries
ports.description: Consecutive failures allowed before the connection gives up and reports an error; 0 keeps retrying
ports.tooltip: 0 means keep retrying. Otherwise the connection reports an error after this many consecutive failures.

ports.name: dedupeById
ports.description: Drops events whose id has already been seen, so a reconnect that resumes cannot re-deliver messages
ports.tooltip: Drop events whose id has already been seen, so a reconnect that resumes from the last event id cannot re-deliver messages. Turn off if your server reuses ids for distinct events.

ports.name: connect
ports.description: Opens the stream, replacing any connection already open and resetting the retry count

ports.name: disconnect
ports.description: Closes the stream and stops retrying

ports.name: connectionState
ports.description: Where the connection is: idle, connecting, open, reconnecting, closed or error

ports.name: connected
ports.description: True only while the stream is open and frames may arrive

ports.name: lastError
ports.description: What went wrong most recently, including the reason a retry was scheduled

ports.name: retryCount
ports.description: Consecutive failed attempts in the current outage; back to zero once the stream opens

ports.name: onOpen
ports.description: Fires when the stream has been established

ports.name: onMessage
ports.description: Fires once per event, after Data, Raw and Text already hold it

ports.name: onError
ports.description: Fires when the stream failed or dropped, whether or not a retry is going to follow

ports.name: onClose
ports.description: Fires when the stream has stopped for good, whether it ended cleanly or gave up

ports.name: done
ports.description: Fires when the action finished: a Connect whose stream opened, or a Disconnect that stopped one

ports.name: completed
ports.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

ports.name: unchanged
ports.description: Fires when there was nothing to do: a Disconnect with no stream running, or a Connect a later Connect or Disconnect superseded before it opened

ports.name: failure
ports.description: Fires when the stream could not be opened, or gave up retrying. Last Error carries the reason

ports.name: data
ports.description: The event payload, parsed as JSON when it is JSON and handed over as text when it is not

ports.name: raw
ports.description: The event payload exactly as it arrived, before any parsing

ports.name: text
ports.description: The one data output guaranteed to be a string: Raw when no Text Path is set, the field at that path when one is, blank when it does not resolve

ports.name: eventType
ports.description: The event name the server sent, or message when it sent none

ports.name: lastEventId
ports.description: The furthest id the server has reported, which is the point a reconnect resumes from

ports.name: messageCount
ports.description: How many events have been delivered on this connection, not counting suppressed duplicates

ports.name: lastMessageTime
ports.description: When the last event arrived, as milliseconds since the epoch; useful for spotting a stalled stream

ports.name: duplicatesSuppressed
ports.description: How many replayed events Dedupe By Id has dropped on this connection

ports.name: deliverySemantics
ports.description: What this stream actually guarantees, derived from whether the server sends ids: at-most-once, at-least-once or at-least-once-deduped

ports.name: chunk
ports.description: The next fragment of text to append; wire a stream Text output, not its Data output, which is JSON-parsed and is usually an object

ports.name: delimiter
ports.description: Message boundary to split complete messages off; leave empty to accumulate everything, which is what a token stream wants
ports.tooltip: Message boundary. Leave empty to accumulate everything without splitting — the mode a token stream wants.

ports.name: maxLength
ports.description: Cap on the pending buffer in characters; overflow drops the oldest and is counted on Dropped Characters
ports.tooltip: Cap on the pending buffer. Overflow drops the oldest characters and is reported on Dropped Characters.

ports.name: maxMessages
ports.description: Cap on retained complete messages, oldest dropped first; 0 keeps them all, which grows forever
ports.tooltip: Cap on retained complete messages; the oldest are dropped first. 0 keeps them all, which grows forever.

ports.name: add
ports.description: Appends the current Chunk, which is retained between pulses, so a second Add with no new chunk appends it again

ports.name: clear
ports.description: Empties the buffer, the messages and both dropped counts

ports.name: accumulated
ports.description: Everything appended since the last Clear that has not yet been split off as a complete message

ports.name: messages
ports.description: Complete messages split off the delimiter, oldest first, capped at Max Messages

ports.name: lastMessage
ports.description: The most recent complete message, which is what a chat surface usually wants

ports.name: messageCount
ports.description: How many complete messages are being retained, which is not how many have arrived

ports.name: characterCount
ports.description: Length of Accumulated in characters

ports.name: byteCount
ports.description: Length of Accumulated in UTF-8 bytes, which differs from Character Count for anything outside ASCII

ports.name: droppedCharacters
ports.description: How many characters Max Length has discarded from the front since the last Clear

ports.name: droppedMessages
ports.description: How many complete messages Max Messages has discarded since the last Clear

ports.name: error
ports.description: Why the last chunk was refused; blank once a chunk of text arrives

ports.name: messageReceived
ports.description: Fires once per Add that completed at least one message, not once per message

ports.name: changed
ports.description: Fires whenever an Add appended something, which is the cue to redraw

ports.name: cleared
ports.description: Fires once the buffer and the messages have been emptied

ports.name: overflowed
ports.description: Fires when Max Length or Max Messages has just discarded something

ports.name: done
ports.description: Fires once an Add or Clear you triggered has changed the buffer

ports.name: completed
ports.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

ports.name: unchanged
ports.description: Fires when an Add had no text to append — an empty chunk, or one already refused — or a Clear found nothing to discard

ports.name: failure
ports.description: Fires when a chunk was not text and nothing was appended, which usually means the wrong stream output is wired

ports.name: chunk
ports.description: The next fragment of the stream; boundaries may fall anywhere, including inside a string

ports.name: format
ports.description: How values are framed on this stream: one per line, any concatenation of complete values, or one whole document

ports.name: maxLength
ports.description: Cap on unparsed text held while a value completes; exceeding it clears the buffer and reports an error rather than growing forever
ports.tooltip: Cap on unparsed text held while waiting for a value to complete. Exceeding it clears the buffer and reports an error, rather than growing without limit on a malformed stream.

ports.name: parse
ports.description: Appends the current Chunk and emits every value that is now complete; the chunk is retained between pulses

ports.name: clear
ports.description: Discards the pending text, the parsed values and the error counter

ports.name: parsed
ports.description: The last complete value the most recent Parse produced

ports.name: values
ports.description: Every value completed by the most recent Parse, in order

ports.name: valueCount
ports.description: How many values have been parsed since the last Clear, across every Parse

ports.name: pendingCharacters
ports.description: Text held back because a value is not complete yet; persistently non-zero means Format does not match the stream

ports.name: isComplete
ports.description: True when the last Parse left nothing pending, so every value so far was whole

ports.name: error
ports.description: Why the last value or line would not parse; kept until the next failure or a Clear

ports.name: errorCount
ports.description: How many values have failed to parse since the last Clear

ports.name: success
ports.description: Fires when a Parse yielded at least one value, so a chunk that merely advanced an incomplete value stays quiet

ports.name: cleared
ports.description: Fires once the pending text and the values have been discarded

ports.name: done
ports.description: Fires when a Parse consumed text or a Clear discarded something; Success is narrower and fires only when values came out

ports.name: completed
ports.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

ports.name: unchanged
ports.description: Fires when there was nothing pending to parse, or nothing to clear — a valid action with nothing to do

ports.name: failure
ports.description: Fires once when a Parse could not read part of its input, or when the pending text exceeded Max Pending; Error Count says how many

ports.name: text
ports.description: The text to search

ports.name: pattern
ports.description: A JavaScript regular expression without the surrounding slashes; capture groups appear on Groups
ports.tooltip: A JavaScript regular expression, without the surrounding slashes. Capture groups appear on Groups.

ports.name: flags
ports.description: Regex flags i, m, s, u and y; g is controlled by Extract All and a g written here is ignored
ports.tooltip: Regex flags: i (ignore case), m (multiline), s (dot matches newline), u (unicode). g is controlled by Extract All.

ports.name: extractAll
ports.description: Collects every match into Matches instead of stopping at the first one

ports.name: extract
ports.description: Runs Pattern over Text and reports what it found

ports.name: match
ports.description: The first match, or blank when nothing matched

ports.name: matches
ports.description: Every match when Extract All is on, otherwise just the first

ports.name: groups
ports.description: Capture groups of the first match; an optional group that did not participate is a blank string, not a hole

ports.name: firstGroup
ports.description: The first capture group of the first match, which is the whole answer for a pattern like (\d+)%

ports.name: namedGroups
ports.description: Named capture groups of the first match, keyed by name

ports.name: matchCount
ports.description: How many matches were found, which is at most one unless Extract All is on

ports.name: error
ports.description: Why the pattern could not be used: it is blank, or it is not a valid regular expression

ports.name: found
ports.description: Fires when the pattern ran and matched at least once

ports.name: notFound
ports.description: Fires when the pattern ran and matched nothing, which is an ordinary outcome rather than a mistake

ports.name: done
ports.description: Fires once the extract has run, whether it matched or not — Found and Not Found say which

ports.name: completed
ports.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

ports.name: failure
ports.description: Fires when the pattern itself is unusable, which is a bug to fix rather than a result

ports.name: data
ports.description: The next item to buffer, of any type; its value is retained between pulses of Add

ports.name: flushSize
ports.description: Flush automatically once this many items are buffered; 0 disables size-based flushing
ports.tooltip: Flush automatically once this many items are buffered. 0 disables size-based flushing.

ports.name: flushInterval
ports.description: Flush automatically this often in milliseconds while items are buffered; 0 disables interval flushing
ports.tooltip: Flush automatically this often while items are buffered. 0 disables interval flushing.

ports.name: maxSize
ports.description: Hard cap on buffered items; overflow drops the oldest and is counted on Dropped Items; 0 means no cap
ports.tooltip: Hard cap on buffered items. Overflow drops the oldest and is reported on Dropped Items. 0 means no cap.

ports.name: add
ports.description: Buffers the current Data, flushing straight away if that reaches Flush Size

ports.name: flush
ports.description: Hands the whole buffer to Flushed Data now; an empty buffer is a legitimate no-op

ports.name: clear
ports.description: Discards the buffer and resets both counters without flushing

ports.name: buffer
ports.description: Items waiting to be flushed, oldest first

ports.name: bufferSize
ports.description: How many items are waiting, which is what Flush Size is compared against

ports.name: flushedData
ports.description: The batch handed over by the most recent flush; a stable array that later Adds do not mutate

ports.name: flushCount
ports.description: How many flushes have happened since the last Clear

ports.name: droppedItems
ports.description: How many items Max Size has discarded from the front since the last Clear

ports.name: flushed
ports.description: Fires once Flushed Data holds a new batch, and not for a flush that found nothing

ports.name: overflowed
ports.description: Fires when Max Size has just discarded something

ports.name: cleared
ports.description: Fires once the buffer has been discarded

ports.name: done
ports.description: Fires once an Add, Flush or Clear you triggered has changed the buffer

ports.name: completed
ports.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

ports.name: unchanged
ports.description: Fires when a Flush found nothing to send, or a Clear found nothing to discard — an idle buffer doing exactly what it should

ports.name: failure
ports.description: Fires when Add ran before any value had arrived on Data, so nothing was buffered

ports.name: error
ports.description: Why the last Add was refused; blank until one is

ports.name: channel
ports.description: Names the handler registry this dispatcher draws on; leave it as default unless two independent flows must not see each other
ports.tooltip: Names the handler registry this dispatcher draws on. Leave as "default" unless two independent flows must not see each other.

ports.name: action
ports.description: An action object, an array of them to run in order, or JSON text holding either
ports.tooltip: An action object, an array of them to run in order, or JSON text holding either.

ports.name: builtIns
ports.description: Comma-separated built-in action names this dispatcher may execute; empty, the default, means a server cannot write to the store at all
ports.tooltip: Comma-separated built-in action names this dispatcher may execute: SET_STORE, MERGE_STORE, DELETE_STORE_KEY, CLEAR_STORE. Empty — the default — means a server cannot write to the store at all; everything must go through an Action Handler you wired.

ports.name: storeName
ports.description: The only store the built-in actions can write; a store named inside an incoming action is ignored
ports.tooltip: The only store the built-in actions can write. A store named inside an incoming action is ignored — the graph chooses the store, not the server.

ports.name: allowedKeys
ports.description: Comma-separated keys the built-in store actions may write; blank means any key, and setting any key also refuses CLEAR_STORE
ports.tooltip: Comma-separated keys the built-in store actions may write. Blank means any key of the configured store. Setting any key also refuses CLEAR_STORE.

ports.name: handlerTimeout
ports.description: Milliseconds a handler has to signal Complete or Fail before the action is failed; 0 waits forever
ports.tooltip: How long a handler has to signal Complete or Fail before the action is failed. 0 waits forever.

ports.name: waitForHandler
ports.description: Milliseconds an action waits for its handler to appear before being refused as unknown; everything behind it waits too
ports.tooltip: How long an action waits for its handler to appear before being refused as unknown — the window in which a component can still mount. 0 refuses immediately. Everything behind it waits too, because order is preserved.

ports.name: maxQueueSize
ports.description: Bound on queued actions; overflow refuses the newest so accepted actions keep their order; 0 is unbounded
ports.tooltip: Bound on queued actions. Overflow refuses the newest so accepted actions keep their order. 0 is unbounded.

ports.name: rateLimit
ports.description: Actions executed per window before the rest are refused rather than delayed; 0 is unlimited
ports.tooltip: Max actions executed per window. 0 is unlimited. Excess actions are refused, not delayed.

ports.name: rateLimitWindow
ports.description: Length of the rate-limit window in milliseconds; ignored unless Rate Limit is set

ports.name: dispatch
ports.description: Admits whatever is on Action and runs it, or refuses it with a reason

ports.name: cancel
ports.description: Discards everything queued and abandons anything in flight, reporting how many were dropped

ports.name: actionType
ports.description: Type of the action currently being executed

ports.name: actionId
ports.description: Id of the action currently being executed, taken from the message when it carried one

ports.name: payload
ports.description: The data the current action carried, taken from its payload or data field, or the whole action when it has neither

ports.name: result
ports.description: What the handler or built-in returned for the action that just completed

ports.name: dispatched
ports.description: Fires when an action has been accepted and is about to run

ports.name: actionCompleted
ports.description: Fires once *one action* has finished and Result holds its answer — one Dispatch of an array fires this once per member, which is why it is not the node’s Completed

ports.name: failed
ports.description: Fires when an accepted action ran and did not succeed, whether the handler said so or the deadline passed

ports.name: idle
ports.description: Fires when the queue has drained after doing at least one thing

ports.name: refused
ports.description: Fires when an action was not run at all, which is the output to watch for anything a server can talk to

ports.name: refusedType
ports.description: Type of the refused action, or blank when the message was too malformed to have one

ports.name: refusalReason
ports.description: Why it was refused, as one of invalid, unknown, not-allowed, rate-limited or queue-full

ports.name: refusalMessage
ports.description: The refusal in a sentence an app author can show or log

ports.name: lastError
ports.description: The most recent failure or refusal, whichever happened last

ports.name: queueSize
ports.description: How many actions are waiting behind the one being executed

ports.name: isExecuting
ports.description: True while an action is running, which is the cue for a busy indicator

ports.name: waitingFor
ports.description: Action type holding the head of the queue because its handler has not registered yet; blank when nothing is waiting

ports.name: completedCount
ports.description: How many actions have completed since the page loaded

ports.name: failedCount
ports.description: How many accepted actions have failed since the page loaded

ports.name: refusedCount
ports.description: How many actions have been refused since the page loaded

ports.name: cancelledCount
ports.description: How many actions Cancel All has discarded since the page loaded

ports.name: cancelled
ports.description: Fires once Cancel All has emptied the queue

ports.name: done
ports.description: Fires when the invocation did something: Dispatch admitted at least one action, or Cancel All dropped at least one

ports.name: completed
ports.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

ports.name: unchanged
ports.description: Fires when there was nothing to do — a Cancel All with an empty queue. Not a failure: the queue is empty, which is what was asked for

ports.name: failure
ports.description: Fires when a Dispatch admitted nothing at all, because every action in it was refused

ports.name: channel
ports.description: Must match the Channel on the Action Dispatcher that should be able to reach this handler
ports.tooltip: Must match the Channel on the Action Dispatcher that should be able to reach this handler.

ports.name: actionType
ports.description: The exact action type this handler accepts; registering it is what makes it executable at all
ports.tooltip: The exact action type this handler accepts, e.g. OPEN_SESSION. Registering it is what makes it executable at all.

ports.name: enabled
ports.description: Turning this off unregisters the handler, so the action is refused as unknown rather than quietly ignored
ports.tooltip: Turning this off unregisters the handler, so the action is refused as unknown rather than quietly ignored.

ports.name: autoComplete
ports.description: Reports the action complete as soon as Trigger has been sent; turn it off when a later step must finish first
ports.tooltip: Report the action complete as soon as Trigger has been sent. Turn off when a later step must wait for this one to finish, and wire Complete or Fail yourself.

ports.name: result
ports.description: Handed back to the dispatcher as the Result of this action when it completes
ports.tooltip: Handed back to the dispatcher as the Result of this action when it completes.

ports.name: errorMessage
ports.description: Reason handed back to the dispatcher when Fail is signalled; a generic one is used when this is blank

ports.name: complete
ports.description: Reports the action finished, so the dispatcher runs whatever is queued behind it; ignored unless Auto Complete is off

ports.name: fail
ports.description: Reports the action failed, so the dispatcher fires Failed with Error Message as the reason

ports.name: trigger
ports.description: Fires when a dispatcher has an action of this type to run; whatever is wired downstream is the capability this grants

ports.name: payload
ports.description: The data the action carried, taken from its payload or data field, or the whole action when it has neither

ports.name: actionId
ports.description: Id of the action currently being handled, so a later Complete can be matched to it

ports.name: registered
ports.description: True while this handler is in the allow-list, which needs both an Action Type and Enabled

ports.name: triggeredCount
ports.description: How many actions this handler has been asked to run since the page loaded

ports.name: error
ports.description: Why the handler could not register, or why the last Complete or Fail had nothing to act on

ports.name: done
ports.description: Fires when Complete or Fail acted on the action in flight — including a Fail, which succeeds by reporting the failure

ports.name: completed
ports.description: Fires after every invocation, whatever the outcome — wire this to carry on regardless. Failure still fires and still carries its reason, so this cannot hide an error

ports.description: Fires when Complete or Fail was signalled with no action in flight

ports.description: Names to pull out of the request body, each becoming an output

ports.name: receive

ports.name: auth

ports.name: userId
ports.description: Id of the user the session token resolved to, and blank for an unauthenticated request
